# Annual Leave and Carry-Forward Policy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how paid annual leave is earned, requested, approved and carried forward at Meridian Technologies. It applies to all permanent employees in India, Singapore and the United Kingdom who are on payroll as of 1 January 2026. Contractors, interns and staff on fixed-term agreements shorter than six months are covered by their engagement letter instead and must not use the leave balances described here. Where a local statutory entitlement exceeds the entitlement in this policy, the statutory minimum applies and the difference is reported by People Operations in the quarterly compliance pack.

## 2. Entitlement

1. Full-time employees accrue 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.
2. Accrual is monthly and pro-rated from the date of joining. An employee joining on the 15th of a month accrues half of that month's entitlement.
3. Part-time employees accrue on a pro-rata basis using contracted hours divided by 40.
4. Employees on probation accrue leave from their first day but may not take more than five days until probation is confirmed.
5. Unused annual leave may be carried forward into the following calendar year up to a maximum of 12 days.
6. Carried-forward days must be used by 31 March of the year into which they were carried. Any balance remaining after 31 March is forfeited without payment in lieu.

Carry-forward is calculated by the payroll system on 31 December and appears on the January payslip. Employees who believe the figure is wrong must raise a ticket with People Operations within 30 days; corrections after that date require Finance approval because the provision has already been booked.

## 3. Requesting leave

1. Leave must be requested in the HR system at least 10 working days before the first day of absence.
2. Requests of five consecutive days or more require approval from the employee's manager and from the department head.
3. Requests spanning a quarter end are automatically routed to the Finance business partner for the department.
4. Leave taken without approval is recorded as unpaid absence until regularised, and regularisation must happen within five working days of return.
5. During a declared incident (Sev-1 or Sev-2), approved leave for on-call staff may be cancelled by the incident commander. Cancelled days are restored in full and are exempt from the carry-forward cap for that year.

## 4. Sick leave and its interaction with annual leave

## 4. Sick leave and its interaction with annual leave

Sick leave is a separate balance of 12 days per year and does not interact with annual leave. An employee who falls ill during approved annual leave may convert the affected days to sick leave by submitting a medical certificate within seven days of returning. Conversion is not available for single-day absences. Sick leave does not carry forward and is not encashed.

1. Employees may encash up to five days of annual leave once per year, in the December payroll cycle.
2. Encashment is paid at basic salary divided by 26.
3. Employees serving notice are not eligible for encashment.
4. Encashment is not available for carried-forward days; only days accrued in the current year may be encashed.

Meridian observes 12 public holidays per year, published each November for the following year. The annual office closure between 24 December and 1 January is not a public holiday; employees must use annual leave for working days in that window unless their team has agreed a coverage rota. Coverage rotas must be published by 1 December and are capped at two consecutive days per employee.

## 7. Transitional provision for long-tenured employees

Employees who joined Meridian before 1 January 2020 retain a grace period for carried-forward leave. For this group only, carried-forward days may be used until 30 April instead of 31 March. This provision was introduced when the leave year was aligned to the calendar year and is reviewed annually by the People Operations committee. It does not extend to days carried forward from a second consecutive year, which lapse on 31 March in all cases. Managers are asked to confirm eligibility in the HR system before approving April leave that draws on a carried balance.

People Operations reports leave liability to Finance monthly. The report includes accrued-but-untaken days, carried-forward days by employee, and days forfeited in the last quarter. Internal Audit samples 25 employees each quarter and checks that approvals exist for every absence longer than three days. Repeated failure to record leave is treated as a performance issue under the Attendance and Timekeeping standard rather than as a disciplinary matter under the Grievance and Discipline policy

## 5. Notice and documentation

1. Employees must notify their manager and People Operations at least 30 days before the intended start date, or as soon as practicable where birth or placement is unexpected.
2. A birth certificate or placement letter must be submitted within 60 days of the start date.
3. Failure to submit documentation within 60 days converts the leave to unpaid until the documentation is received; the leave is then reinstated retrospectively.

## 6. Top-up and benefits during leave

Employees may top up statutory pay to full salary using accrued annual leave or, where the statutory scheme pays less than base salary, through the salary top-up scheme described in Appendix B. Health insurance continues uninterrupted for the employee and dependants. Pension contributions continue at the employee's pre-leave rate for the full duration of paid leave. Annual leave accrues during parental leave at the normal monthly rate but may not be taken until the employee returns.

## 7. Return to work

1. Employees are entitled to a phased return of up to four weeks at 60% workload with full pay.

# Exit and Separation Policy

## 1. Scope

This policy covers resignation, termination, redundancy and retirement for all permanent employees. It does not cover contractors, whose notice terms are in their engagement letter.

## 2. Notice periods

1. Employees at L4 and above serve 60 days' notice.
2. Employees at L1 to L3 serve 30 days' notice.
3. Employees in their first 90 days serve 15 days' notice.
4. Notice runs from the day after the written resignation is acknowledged by the manager and People Operations. Verbal notice does not start the clock.
5. Meridian may pay salary in lieu of notice, in whole or in part, at its discretion.

## 3. Resignation process

1. Submit resignation in the HR system and inform the manager in writing.
2. People Operations acknowledges within two working days and confirms the last working day.
3. Knowledge transfer is agreed with the manager within five working days.
4. The employee must return all company property, including the laptop, badge and any storage media, on or before the last working day.
5. Access to systems is removed at 18:00 on the last working day unless a shorter period is required for security.

## 4. Exit interview

An exit interview is offered to every departing employee and is scheduled within five working days of the last day. It is conducted by People Operations, not by the manager. Responses are aggregated quarterly and are never attributed to an individual without consent. Attendance is voluntary and does not affect final settlement.

## 5. Final settlement

1. Final salary, leave encashment and any approved reimbursements are paid within 45 days of the last working day.
2. Leave encashment follows HR_Leave_Policy: up to five accrued days, not carried-forward days.

## 6. Redundancy

Redundancy requires a business case approved by the Chief People Officer and the CEO. Employees selected for redundancy receive the statutory notice or pay in lieu, plus a severance of one month's base salary per completed year of service, capped at six months. Redeployment is attempted for 30 days before redundancy is confirmed.

# Cafeteria Catering Standards

## 1. Service hours

The Pune cafeteria serves breakfast 08:00–10:30, lunch 12:00–14:30 and snacks 16:00–17:30. The vendor must publish the weekly menu every Friday for the following week.

## 2. Dietary requirements

Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options must be available at every meal. Allergen labelling is mandatory at the counter. Jain options are available on request with one day's notice.

## 3. Hygiene

The vendor holds a valid food safety licence and undergoes a quarterly hygiene audit. Temperature logs are kept for all cooked and chilled items. Staff handling food must hold a current health certificate.

## 4. Subsidy

Meridian subsidises lunch up to INR 120 per employee per working day. The subsidy is applied at the till by badge. Guests pay full price.

The menu rotates on a four-week cycle and repeats no main dish within two weeks. Each day offers at least two vegetarian mains, one non-vegetarian main, a salad, a soup and a dessert. Fried items appear no more than twice a week.

The vendor submits the following week's menu by Friday for Facilities approval. Changes after approval are allowed only for supply reasons and are announced at the counter and on the internal notice.

# Subpoena and Litigation Hold

## 1. Immediate steps

1. Anyone who receives a subpoena, court order, regulatory request or formal notice of a dispute must notify Legal within 24 hours.
2. Do not respond to the requester, confirm receipt, or discuss the matter outside Legal.
3. Do not delete, edit or move any related record, including chat messages, emails and tickets.

1. Legal issues a written hold to the custodians it identifies.
2. Custodians must acknowledge the hold within two business days.

4. IT must suspend mailbox and backup deletion for the named custodians until Legal releases the hold.

Legal releases the hold in writing when the matter concludes. Normal retention resumes from the release date, and the retention clock is not shortened by the hold period.

Every piece of information Meridian holds has a classification. The classification determines who may access it, how it must be stored and shared, and how long it is kept. When in doubt, classify higher and ask the data owner; misclassifying downward is a security incident.

# Data Privacy and GDPR Compliance

## 1. Scope

This policy governs the processing of personal data of customers, employees, candidates and website visitors. It applies to every team and every system, including systems bought by a department without Legal involvement. Where local law is stricter than this policy, the stricter rule applies.

## 2. Lawful basis

Every processing activity needs a lawful basis recorded in the processing register: contract, legal obligation, legitimate interest, consent or vital interest. Marketing consent must be opt-in and separately recorded; pre-ticked boxes are not consent. Legitimate interest assessments are documented by the DPO.

## 3. Data subject rights

1. A data subject access request (DSAR) must be answered within 30 days of receipt.

3. Identity must be verified before data is released; verification must not require excessive documentation.

## 4. Breach notification

2. The DPO assesses whether the breach is notifiable; a notifiable breach is reported to the regulator within 72 hours.
3. Affected individuals are informed without undue delay where the breach is likely to result in high risk.
4. A breach log is maintained for five years.

## 5. Vendors and transfers

Vendors processing personal data require a Data Processing Agreement under IT_Vendor_Security_Review. Transfers outside the EEA require an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses. A transfer impact assessment is required for any new destination country.

New systems and features must complete a data protection impact assessment before launch where they process sensitive data, profile individuals or use new technology. The DPIA is reviewed by the DPO and stored with the project record.

All employees complete privacy training annually. The DPO audits two teams per quarter against the processing register and reports findings to the audit committee.

# Vendor Security Review

## 1. When a review is required

Any third party that will store, process or access Meridian data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. This includes SaaS tools, contractors with system access, managed services and data processors. A review is not required for vendors that receive only Public information, but the classification must be recorded.

## 2. Process and timelines

1. The business owner submits the vendor request with the intended data classification and integration scope.
2. Security Engineering sends the standard questionnaire within 2 working days.
3. The vendor returns the questionnaire and evidence. The review concludes within 30 days of receiving complete evidence.
4. Reviews requiring a penetration test summary or a Data Processing Agreement take up to 45 days.
5. Contracts must not be signed before the review is recorded as passed.

## 3. Evidence requirements

1. SOC 2 Type II is required for any vendor processing Confidential or Restricted data. A SOC 2 Type I is accepted only with a remediation plan and a follow-up date.
2. ISO 27001 certification is accepted in place of SOC 2 where the scope covers the service in question.
3. Vendors without either certification require a documented compensating review by Security Engineering and approval from the CTO.
4. Encryption at rest and in transit must be evidenced.
5. Sub-processors must be listed and approved; unreported sub-processors are a contractual breach.

## 4. Data processing terms

Where personal data is involved, Legal_Data_Privacy_GDPR_Compliance requires a Data Processing Agreement. The DPA must cover purpose limitation, breach notification within 72 hours, deletion on termination and audit rights. Vendors that cannot accept the standard terms are escalated to Legal.

1. Confidential and Restricted vendors are reassessed annually.

An exception requires the CTO's written approval, a compensating control and an expiry date no later than 90 days. Exceptions are reported to the security committee monthly.

This policy sets out how paid annual leave is earned, requested, approved and carried forward at Meridian Technologies. ## 1. Purpose

This runbook defines who is paged, in what order, and how quickly a bridge must open when a production or customer-facing incident is declared. It is the operational companion to IT_Incident_Response_Runbook, which defines severity and the postmortem process.

Runbook version 1.4, in force from January 2025 until February 2026, required the incident bridge to open within 10 minutes of declaration. Pages go through the on-call tool, not direct messages. If the first page is not acknowledged within the window, the tool automatically escalates to the next level. Escalation does not stop when someone joins the bridge; it stops when the incident commander is confirmed.

Any engineer may declare a Sev-1. Downgrading requires the incident commander and the engineering director. Repeatedly downgrading to avoid the bridge requirement is reviewed by Reliability Engineering.

A postmortem is due within 5 business days.

# Vendor Payment Terms

## 1. Default terms

1. The default payment term for vendor invoices is Net 45 from the invoice date.
2. The invoice date is the date the invoice is issued, not the date it is received.
3. Payment runs happen twice a month, on the 10th and the 25th. An invoice falling due between runs is paid on the next run.
4. Vendors must quote a purchase order number on every invoice; invoices without one are returned unpaid.

## 2. Early payment discount

1. Where a vendor offers a 2% discount for payment within 10 days, Accounts Payable takes the discount if the cash position allows.
2. The discount is calculated on the invoice value excluding taxes.
3. Discounts are recorded as a separate line in the vendor ledger, not netted against the payable.
4. Vendors offering a discount for payment within 5 days are reviewed by the treasury team before acceptance.

## 3. Invoice validation

1. A three-way match is required: purchase order, goods receipt and invoice.
2. Mismatches are resolved with the business owner within 5 working days.
3. Invoices above INR 10,00,000 require a second Finance review.
4. Duplicate invoices are flagged by the vendor ledger and are never paid twice.

## 4. Late payment

1. Interest is payable on late invoices at 1% per month where the delay exceeds 30 days beyond the agreed term.
2. Interest is not payable where the delay is caused by a missing purchase order or a disputed invoice.
3. Persistent late payment is reported to the CFO monthly.

## 5. Small invoices

Invoices below INR 5,00,000 are settled on Net 30 rather than Net 45. This exception exists to reduce the administrative cost of low-value payables and does not require a contract amendment. Where a contract states Net 45 for a vendor whose invoices are consistently below the threshold, Accounts Payable applies Net 30 and records the deviation in the vendor file. Business owners should expect the shorter term when planning cash.

## 6. Foreign currency

Foreign currency invoices are paid in the invoice currency. The exchange rate is the bank rate on the payment date. Vendors may not require payment in a currency other than the contract currency.

- Finance_Procurement_Approval_Matrix for purchase orders.
- IT_Vendor_Security_Review for data-handling

# Revenue Recognition Policy

## 1. Principle

Revenue is recognised when control of the promised service passes to the customer, in the amount the company expects to be entitled to. Meridian applies the five-step model: identify the contract, identify the performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the price to the obligations, and recognise revenue as each obligation is satisfied.

## 2. Contract identification

A contract exists when it is approved, the rights and payment terms are identifiable, it has commercial substance, and collection is probable. Orders below INR 1,00,000 with a standard online acceptance are treated as contracts on acceptance. Deals with non-standard terms require Legal_Contract_Review_Process before revenue can be scheduled.

## 3. Performance obligations

1. Subscription access is a series of distinct daily services recognised over the contract term.
2. Implementation services are a separate obligation when the customer can benefit from them independently; otherwise they are combined with the subscription.
3. Training is a separate obligation recognised when delivered.
4. Hardware resold with software is recognised on delivery.

## 4. Transaction price

1. The transaction price includes fixed fees and variable consideration that is probable and estimable.
2. Discounts are allocated proportionally across obligations unless the contract evidences a standalone price for one obligation.
3. Rebates and service credits are estimated and constrained until the uncertainty resolves.
4. Significant financing components are adjusted where payment terms exceed 12 months.

## 5. Milestone and deferred revenue

1. Annual prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and released monthly over the term.
2. Milestone billing on implementation is recognised against delivery of the milestone, not against the invoice date.
3. Where a milestone is invoiced before delivery, the balance sits in deferred revenue.
4. Where delivery precedes invoicing, an unbilled receivable is recorded.

## 6. Contract modifications

A modification is treated as a separate contract if it adds distinct services priced at standalone selling price. Otherwise the remaining consideration is reallocated over the remaining obligations. Modifications must be documented by the deal desk and approved by the Controller.

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.

# Annual Leave and Carry-Forward Policy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how paid annual leave is earned, requested, approved and carried forward at Meridian Technologies. It applies to all permanent employees in India, Singapore and the United Kingdom who are on payroll as of 1 January 2026. Contractors, interns and staff on fixed-term agreements shorter than six months are covered by their engagement letter instead and must not use the leave balances described here. Where a local statutory entitlement exceeds the entitlement in this policy, the statutory minimum applies and the difference is reported by People Operations in the quarterly compliance pack.

## 2. Entitlement

1. Full-time employees accrue 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.
2. Accrual is monthly and pro-rated from the date of joining. An employee joining on the 15th of a month accrues half of that month's entitlement.
3. Part-time employees accrue on a pro-rata basis using contracted hours divided by 40.
4. Employees on probation accrue leave from their first day but may not take more than five days until probation is confirmed.
5. Unused annual leave may be carried forward into the following calendar year up to a maximum of 12 days.
6. Carried-forward days must be used by 31 March of the year into which they were carried. Any balance remaining after 31 March is forfeited without payment in lieu.

Carry-forward is calculated by the payroll system on 31 December and appears on the January payslip. Employees who believe the figure is wrong must raise a ticket with People Operations within 30 days; corrections after that date require Finance approval because the provision has already been booked.

## 3. Requesting leave

1. Leave must be requested in the HR system at least 10 working days before the first day of absence.
2. Requests of five consecutive days or more require approval from the employee's manager and from the department head.
3. Requests spanning a quarter end are automatically routed to the Finance business partner for the department.
4. Leave taken without approval is recorded as unpaid absence until regularised, and regularisation must happen within five working days of return.
5. During a declared incident (Sev-1 or Sev-2), approved leave for on-call staff may be cancelled by the incident commander. Cancelled days are restored in full and are exempt from the carry-forward cap for that year.

Sick leave is a separate balance of 12 days per year and does not interact with annual leave. An employee who falls ill during approved annual leave may convert the affected days to sick leave by submitting a medical certificate within seven days of returning. Conversion is not available for single-day absences. Sick leave does not carry forward and is not encashed.

1. Employees may encash up to five days of annual leave once per year, in the December payroll cycle.
2. Encashment is paid at basic salary divided by 26.

Meridian observes 12 public holidays per year, published each November for the following year. # Parental Leave Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy sets out paid leave for birth, adoption and surrogacy for all permanent employees who have completed 90 days of continuous service. It applies equally to all genders; the entitlement depends on the caregiving role the employee declares, not on the employee's gender or the child's origin. Employees on fixed-term contracts of 12 months or more receive the same entitlement pro-rated to their remaining contract length.

## 2. Primary caregiver entitlement

1. A primary caregiver is entitled to 26 weeks of paid parental leave.
2. Leave may begin up to four weeks before the expected date of birth or the date of adoption placement.
3. Leave must be taken in a single continuous block. Splitting into two blocks is permitted only where the second block is taken within 12 months of the birth and the manager and People Operations both approve in writing.
4. Pay during primary caregiver leave is 100% of base salary for the first 26 weeks.
5. The employee returns to the same role and grade. If the role has been made redundant during the leave, the redundancy process must follow the Exit and Separation policy and the employee is entitled to redeployment priority for 90 days.

## 3. Secondary caregiver entitlement

1. A secondary caregiver is entitled to 6 weeks of paid parental leave.
2. Secondary leave may be taken in up to three blocks within 12 months of the birth or placement.
3. Pay during secondary caregiver leave is 100% of base salary.
4. A secondary caregiver may switch to primary caregiver status once, by written declaration, provided fewer than 13 weeks of the primary entitlement have been used. The switch requires People Operations approval and is recorded in the HR system.

## 4. Adoption and surrogacy

1. Adoption is treated identically to birth for both entitlements.
2. Leave may begin on the date the child is placed with the employee, not the date the adoption is legally finalised.
3. Employees pursuing surrogacy are entitled to the secondary caregiver entitlement, and to the primary entitlement where they are the sole intended parent.
4. Documentation required: placement letter from the adoption agency or a surrogacy agreement summary. Medical details are never required.

# Exit and Separation Policy

## 1. Scope

This policy covers resignation, termination, redundancy and retirement for all permanent employees. It does not cover contractors, whose notice terms are in their engagement letter.

## 2. Notice periods

1. Employees at L4 and above serve 60 days' notice.
2. Employees at L1 to L3 serve 30 days' notice.
3. Employees in their first 90 days serve 15 days' notice.
4. Notice runs from the day after the written resignation is acknowledged by the manager and People Operations. Verbal notice does not start the clock.
5. Meridian may pay salary in lieu of notice, in whole or in part, at its discretion.

## 3. Resignation process

1. Submit resignation in the HR system and inform the manager in writing.
2. People Operations acknowledges within two working days and confirms the last working day.
3. Knowledge transfer is agreed with the manager within five working days.
4. The employee must return all company property, including the laptop, badge and any storage media, on or before the last working day.
5. Access to systems is removed at 18:00 on the last working day unless a shorter period is required for security.

## 4. Exit interview

An exit interview is offered to every departing employee and is scheduled within five working days of the last day. It is conducted by People Operations, not by the manager. Responses are aggregated quarterly and are never attributed to an individual without consent. Attendance is voluntary and does not affect final settlement.

## 5. Final settlement

1. Final salary, leave encashment and any approved reimbursements are paid within 45 days of the last working day.
2. Leave encashment follows HR_Leave_Policy: up to five accrued days, not carried-forward days.
3. Sign-on or relocation bonuses subject to a clawback are recovered from the final settlement where the clawback period has not elapsed.
4. Disputed amounts are raised with Payroll within 30 days of the settlement statement.

## 6. Redundancy

Redundancy requires a business case approved by the Chief People Officer and the CEO. Employees selected for redundancy receive the statutory notice or pay in lieu, plus a severance of one month's base salary per completed year of service, capped at six months. Redeployment is attempted for 30 days before redundancy is confirmed.

## 8. Alumni and references

Departing employees in good standing are added to the alumni network. References confirm dates of employment and job title only; managers do not provide character references on company letterhead.

# Annual Leave and Carry-Forward Policy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how paid annual leave is earned, requested, approved and carried forward at Meridian Technologies. It applies to all permanent employees in India, Singapore and the United Kingdom who are on payroll as of 1 January 2026. Contractors, interns and staff on fixed-term agreements shorter than six months are covered by their engagement letter instead and must not use the leave balances described here. Where a local statutory entitlement exceeds the entitlement in this policy, the statutory minimum applies and the difference is reported by People Operations in the quarterly compliance pack.

## 2. Entitlement

1. Full-time employees accrue 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.
2. Accrual is monthly and pro-rated from the date of joining. An employee joining on the 15th of a month accrues half of that month's entitlement.
3. Part-time employees accrue on a pro-rata basis using contracted hours divided by 40.
4. Employees on probation accrue leave from their first day but may not take more than five days until probation is confirmed.
5. Unused annual leave may be carried forward into the following calendar year up to a maximum of 12 days.
6. Carried-forward days must be used by 31 March of the year into which they were carried. Any balance remaining after 31 March is forfeited without payment in lieu.

Carry-forward is calculated by the payroll system on 31 December and appears on the January payslip. Employees who believe the figure is wrong must raise a ticket with People Operations within 30 days; corrections after that date require Finance approval because the provision has already been booked.

## 3. Requesting leave

1. Leave must be requested in the HR system at least 10 working days before the first day of absence.
2. Requests of five consecutive days or more require approval from the employee's manager and from the department head.
3. Requests spanning a quarter end are automatically routed to the Finance business partner for the department.
4. Leave taken without approval is recorded as unpaid absence until regularised, and regularisation must happen within five working days of return.
5. During a declared incident (Sev-1 or Sev-2), approved leave for on-call staff may be cancelled by the incident commander. Cancelled days are restored in full and are exempt from the carry-forward cap for that year.

## 4. Sick leave and its interaction with annual leave

## 4. Sick leave and its interaction with annual leave

Sick leave is a separate balance of 12 days per year and does not interact with annual leave. An employee who falls ill during approved annual leave may convert the affected days to sick leave by submitting a medical certificate within seven days of returning. Conversion is not available for single-day absences. Sick leave does not carry forward and is not encashed.

## 5. Encashment

1. Employees may encash up to five days of annual leave once per year, in the December payroll cycle.
2. Encashment is paid at basic salary divided by 26.
3. Employees serving notice are not eligible for encashment.
4. Encashment is not available for carried-forward days; only days accrued in the current year may be encashed.

## 6. Public holidays and office closures

Meridian observes 12 public holidays per year, published each November for the following year. The annual office closure between 24 December and 1 January is not a public holiday; employees must use annual leave for working days in that window unless their team has agreed a coverage rota. Coverage rotas must be published by 1 December and are capped at two consecutive days per employee.

## 7. Transitional provision for long-tenured employees

Employees who joined Meridian before 1 January 2020 retain a grace period for carried-forward leave. For this group only, carried-forward days may be used until 30 April instead of 31 March. This provision was introduced when the leave year was aligned to the calendar year and is reviewed annually by the People Operations committee. It does not extend to days carried forward from a second consecutive year, which lapse on 31 March in all cases. Managers are asked to confirm eligibility in the HR system before approving April leave that draws on a carried balance.

## 8. Records, reporting and audit

People Operations reports leave liability to Finance monthly. The report includes accrued-but-untaken days, carried-forward days by employee, and days forfeited in the last quarter. Internal Audit samples 25 employees each quarter and checks that approvals exist for every absence longer than three days. Repeated failure to record leave is treated as a performance issue under the Attendance and Timekeeping standard rather than as a disciplinary matter under the Grievance and Discipline policy

## Annex A. Onboarding stages

Onboarding runs through five stages: contract handover, environment provisioning, data import, configuration and acceptance, and go-live handover. Each stage has an owner, a definition of done and a checkpoint in the onboarding tracker. The 14-day clock covers all five stages from the complete setup package.

The package is checked against a checklist at handover from Sales. Missing items are requested in one message listing everything outstanding, and the clock does not start until they arrive. Sales is told that the clock has not started so the customer conversation stays accurate.

Provisioning is automated for standard tenants and takes under a day. Data import depends on the customer's export, and the specification is agreed before the clock starts so the import does not stall halfway.

Acceptance is a scripted walkthrough with the customer's admin covering sign-in, user provisioning, the three most-used workflows and the audit log. Acceptance is confirmed by email, and the handover email starts the support relationship.

Credits are calculated by Customer Operations from the tracker rather than negotiated case by case: five percent from day 15, ten percent from day 31, shown on the next invoice with a reference to this policy.

Monthly reporting counts only accounts where the clock ran, states the median days to live and lists every credited account with its cause.

## 5. Security requirements

Remote work is subject to the IT_Access_Control_Standard and the IT_Acceptable_Use_Policy. In summary: company laptops only, full-disk encryption enabled, VPN required for internal systems, no work on public or shared computers, and screens must not be visible to others in public spaces. Confidential material must not be printed at home. A security incident arising from a remote workspace must be reported within one hour to the security team.

## 6. Cross-border remote work

Working from another country is not covered by this policy and requires a separate tax and immigration review led by People Operations. Requests must be raised 45 days in advance. Approval is limited to 20 working days per year and is not available to employees in Finance, Legal or Payroll because of data residency constraints.

## 7. Attendance and performance

Remote work does not change performance expectations. Managers assess output, not presence. Persistent failure to meet agreed deliverables while remote is handled under the Performance Review Process, not by withdrawing remote eligibility as a disciplinary measure. Withdrawal of eligibility requires a documented business reason and 30 days' notice.

## 8. Hybrid meetings

Every meeting with at least one remote participant must have a video link, a shared agenda and a designated note-taker. Decisions must be written in the meeting notes within one working day. Whiteboard-only sessions must be photographed and shared.

## 5. Notice and documentation

1. Employees must notify their manager and People Operations at least 30 days before the intended start date, or as soon as practicable where birth or placement is unexpected.
2. A birth certificate or placement letter must be submitted within 60 days of the start date.
3. Failure to submit documentation within 60 days converts the leave to unpaid until the documentation is received; the leave is then reinstated retrospectively.

## 6. Top-up and benefits during leave

Employees may top up statutory pay to full salary using accrued annual leave or, where the statutory scheme pays less than base salary, through the salary top-up scheme described in Appendix B. Health insurance continues uninterrupted for the employee and dependants. Pension contributions continue at the employee's pre-leave rate for the full duration of paid leave. Annual leave accrues during parental leave at the normal monthly rate but may not be taken until the employee returns.

## 7. Return to work

1. Employees are entitled to a phased return of up to four weeks at 60% workload with full pay.
2. A return-to-work conversation with the manager must happen in the two weeks before the return date.
3. Nursing employees are entitled to two 30-minute breaks per working day for 12 months after the birth.
4. Travel requirements are waived for the first eight weeks after return.

## 8. Interaction with other leave

Parental leave does not reduce annual leave entitlement. Sick leave taken during parental leave is recorded separately and does not extend the parental leave period. Parental leave counts as continuous service for the purpose of the Employee Referral Program and the Learning and Development budget.

This policy covers resignation, termination, redundancy and retirement for all permanent employees. It does not cover contractors, whose notice terms are in their engagement letter.

# Records Retention Schedule

## 1. Purpose

This schedule states how long each category of record is kept and when the retention clock starts. Keeping records longer than necessary creates privacy and discovery risk; deleting them early breaches legal obligations. Where two rules conflict, the longer period applies.

## 2. Schedule

| Record category | Retention period | Clock starts |
|---|---|---|
| Executed contracts | 8 years | Contract expiry or termination |
| Contract drafts and redlines | 3 years | Contract signature |
| Payroll and tax records | 7 years | End of the tax year |
| Employee personnel files | 7 years | Last working day |
| Recruitment records | 1 year | Application date |
| Incident logs and postmortems | 3 years | Incident resolution |
| Security access logs | 1 year | Log creation |
| Financial statements and audit files | 8 years | End of the financial year |
| Privacy breach log | 5 years | Breach discovery |
| Vendor due diligence | 6 years | Engagement end |

## 3. Application

1. The clock starts on the trigger event, not on the date the record was created.
2. A legal hold suspends deletion for the affected records under Legal_Subpoena_And_Litigation_Hold.
3. Records past their retention period are deleted during the quarterly purge run by the record owner.
4. Deletion of Confidential or Restricted records requires a certificate under IT_Data_Classification_Standard.

## 4. Legal holds

When a hold is issued, the record owner must stop all deletion immediately, including automated purge jobs, and confirm compliance in writing within two business days. The hold overrides this schedule until Legal releases it in writing.

## 5. Exceptions

An exception to shorten retention requires the Head of Legal's approval and must be recorded with the reason. Exceptions to lengthen retention are granted for litigation, investigations and regulatory requests.

## 6. Related documents

- IT_Data_Classification_Standard for disposal.
- Legal_Data_Privacy_GDPR_Compliance for erasure requests.
- Finance_Fiscal_Year_2026_Audit_Prep for audit evidence.
- HR_Exit_And_Separation for personnel files.

## 1. Service hours

The Pune cafeteria serves breakfast 08:00–10:30, lunch 12:00–14:30 and snacks 16:00–17:30. The vendor must publish the weekly menu every Friday for the following week.

Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options must be available at every meal. Allergen labelling is mandatory at the counter. Jain options are available on request with one day's notice.

The vendor holds a valid food safety licence and undergoes a quarterly hygiene audit. Temperature logs are kept for all cooked and chilled items. Staff handling food must hold a current health certificate.

Meridian subsidises lunch up to INR 120 per employee per working day. The subsidy is applied at the till by badge. Guests pay full price.

Desks are not assigned. Teams receive a neighbourhood and book desks through the facilities system. Bookings open 14 days ahead and expire at 10:30 on the booked day if not checked in. Meeting rooms are booked separately. Employees who attend fewer than the required days release their desk booking priority to colleagues who attend more.

## 6. Compliance

1. People Operations reports attendance to department heads monthly.
2. A first month below the minimum triggers a conversation with the manager.
3. Three consecutive months below the minimum without an approved accommodation is treated as a performance matter and handled under HR

# Anti-Corruption Compliance

## 1. Policy statement

Meridian prohibits bribery in any form, in any country. This includes offering, promising, authorising or accepting anything of value to obtain or retain business or an improper advantage. The policy applies to employees, contractors, agents, distributors and anyone acting on Meridian's behalf.

## 2. Gifts and hospitality

1. Gifts to or from business partners must be under INR 5,000 in value.
2. Gifts above that value must be declined or surrendered to People Operations.
3. Cash and cash equivalents are never permitted.
4. Hospitality must be modest, infrequent, recorded in the gifts register and approved by a manager.
5. Nothing may be given to a government official, including meals, travel or event tickets, without Legal's written approval.

## 3. Facilitation payments

Facilitation payments — small payments to speed up a routine government action — are prohibited even where local practice expects them. An employee asked for one must refuse, report it to Legal and document the request.

## 4. Third parties

1. Agents, distributors and consultants are subject to due diligence before engagement and every two years afterwards.
2. Due diligence covers ownership, reputation, government connections and sanctions screening.
3. Contracts must include anti-corruption representations, audit rights and termination for breach.
4. Payments to third parties must be made to the contracting entity in the contract country; payments to offshore accounts require Legal approval.

## 5. Political and charitable contributions

Company political contributions are not permitted. Charitable donations require CEO approval and must not be made at the request of a government official or a customer.

## 6. Red flags

Unusual payment routes, requests for cash, invoices without deliverables, unusually high commissions, and a refusal to sign anti-corruption terms are red flags. Any red flag must be reported to Legal before the transaction proceeds.

## 7. Reporting and consequences

Reports may go to a manager, Legal or the ethics line and may be anonymous. Retaliation is prohibited. Breach of this policy may result in termination and referral to authorities.

# Vendor Payment Terms

## 1. Default terms

1. The default payment term for vendor invoices is Net 45 from the invoice date.
2. The invoice date is the date the invoice is issued, not the date it is received.
3. Payment runs happen twice a month, on the 10th and the 25th. An invoice falling due between runs is paid on the next run.
4. Vendors must quote a purchase order number on every invoice; invoices without one are returned unpaid.

## 2. Early payment discount

1. Where a vendor offers a 2% discount for payment within 10 days, Accounts Payable takes the discount if the cash position allows.
2. The discount is calculated on the invoice value excluding taxes.
3. Discounts are recorded as a separate line in the vendor ledger, not netted against the payable.
4. Vendors offering a discount for payment within 5 days are reviewed by the treasury team before acceptance.

## 3. Invoice validation

1. A three-way match is required: purchase order, goods receipt and invoice.
2. Mismatches are resolved with the business owner within 5 working days.
3. Invoices above INR 10,00,000 require a second Finance review.
4. Duplicate invoices are flagged by the vendor ledger and are never paid twice.

## 4. Late payment

1. Interest is payable on late invoices at 1% per month where the delay exceeds 30 days beyond the agreed term.
2. Interest is not payable where the delay is caused by a missing purchase order or a disputed invoice.
3. Persistent late payment is reported to the CFO monthly.

## 5. Small invoices

Invoices below INR 5,00,000 are settled on Net 30 rather than Net 45. This exception exists to reduce the administrative cost of low-value payables and does not require a contract amendment. Where a contract states Net 45 for a vendor whose invoices are consistently below the threshold, Accounts Payable applies Net 30 and records the deviation in the vendor file. Business owners should expect the shorter term when planning cash.

## 6. Foreign currency

Foreign currency invoices are paid in the invoice currency. The exchange rate is the bank rate on the payment date. Vendors may not require payment in a currency other than the contract currency.

- Finance_Procurement_Approval_Matrix for purchase orders.
- IT_Vendor_Security_Review for data-handling

## 1. Cycle

Meridian runs two review cycles per year. The mid-year cycle covers January to June and concludes in July. The annual cycle covers July to December and concludes in January, and it is the cycle that drives salary and bonus decisions under HR_Compensation_Bands. # Severity Incident Escalation

## 1. Purpose

This runbook defines who is paged, in what order, and how quickly a bridge must open when a production or customer-facing incident is declared. It is the operational companion to IT_Incident_Response_Runbook, which defines severity and the postmortem process.

## 2. Bridge requirement

Runbook version 1.4, in force from January 2025 until February 2026, required the incident bridge to open within 10 minutes of declaration. This version (2.0) requires the bridge to open within 15 minutes, because the 10-minute target produced incomplete bridges while pages were still in flight. The 15-minute window is the current standard and applies to every Sev-1, including security incidents.

## 3. Escalation matrix

| Severity | First page | Second page (after) | Executive notified |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sev-1 | On-call engineer, on-call manager | Engineering director (15 min) | CTO (30 min) |
| Sev-2 | On-call engineer | On-call manager (30 min) | Department head (2 h) |
| Sev-3 | On-call engineer | Team lead (next business day) | No |

Pages go through the on-call tool, not direct messages. If the first page is not acknowledged within the window, the tool automatically escalates to the next level. Escalation does not stop when someone joins the bridge; it stops when the incident commander is confirmed.

## 4. Roles on the bridge

The incident commander owns coordination and communication. The communications lead writes customer updates. The scribe keeps the timeline. Subject-matter engineers investigate. For a Sev-1 the incident commander must be an engineering manager or above; for a Sev-2 the on-call engineer may take the role.

## 5. Communication cadence

Internal updates every 30 minutes for a Sev-1 and every 2 hours for a Sev-2. Customer updates follow IT_Incident_Response_Runbook. No root-cause speculation in customer communication.

## 6. Declaring and downgrading

Any engineer may declare a Sev-1. Downgrading requires the incident commander and the engineering director. Repeatedly downgrading to avoid the bridge requirement is reviewed by Reliability Engineering.

## 7. After the incident

A postmortem is due within 5 business days.

# Travel Insurance FAQ

## 1. Do I need to buy travel insurance?

No. Corporate travel cover applies automatically to every business trip booked through the corporate travel tool. Buying separate cover is not reimbursable.

## 2. What is covered?

Medical treatment and evacuation up to USD 250,000, trip cancellation, baggage loss up to USD 1,500, and personal liability. Pre-existing conditions are covered for business travel only.

## 3. How do I claim?

Call the insurer's assistance line before any treatment. Keep every receipt and submit the claim within 30 days of returning. Finance can provide the policy number and the assistance card.

## 4. Leisure add-ons

Extending a trip for leisure is allowed with manager approval, but the leisure portion is not covered and any change fee is personal.

Cover begins when the trip is booked through the corporate travel tool and ends when the traveller returns to their home city. Personal days attached to a business trip are not covered, including the gap between the business purpose ending and the return flight.

Rooms are booked through the calendar system. Bookings open 14 days ahead and are limited to 4 hours per booking. Recurring bookings are limited to 8 weeks and must be re-confirmed afterwards.

A room not occupied within 10 minutes of the booking start is released automatically. Three no-shows in a month remove booking rights for the following month.

## 3. Room types

Focus rooms seat 2 and have no video equipment. Huddle rooms seat 6 with video. Training rooms seat 24 and require Facilities approval. The boardroom is reserved for customer meetings and executive sessions.

Bookings are for the booker's own meetings. Booking for a colleague is not allowed, and an event that names another organiser is transferred rather than duplicated. Rooms are not booked for personal use or to hold a desk.

# Revenue Recognition Policy

## 1. Principle

Revenue is recognised when control of the promised service passes to the customer, in the amount the company expects to be entitled to. Meridian applies the five-step model: identify the contract, identify the performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the price to the obligations, and recognise revenue as each obligation is satisfied.

## 2. Contract identification

A contract exists when it is approved, the rights and payment terms are identifiable, it has commercial substance, and collection is probable. Orders below INR 1,00,000 with a standard online acceptance are treated as contracts on acceptance. Deals with non-standard terms require Legal_Contract_Review_Process before revenue can be scheduled.

## 3. Performance obligations

1. Subscription access is a series of distinct daily services recognised over the contract term.
2. Implementation services are a separate obligation when the customer can benefit from them independently; otherwise they are combined with the subscription.
3. Training is a separate obligation recognised when delivered.
4. Hardware resold with software is recognised on delivery.

## 4. Transaction price

1. The transaction price includes fixed fees and variable consideration that is probable and estimable.
2. Discounts are allocated proportionally across obligations unless the contract evidences a standalone price for one obligation.
3. Rebates and service credits are estimated and constrained until the uncertainty resolves.
4. Significant financing components are adjusted where payment terms exceed 12 months.

## 5. Milestone and deferred revenue

1. Annual prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and released monthly over the term.
2. Milestone billing on implementation is recognised against delivery of the milestone, not against the invoice date.
3. Where a milestone is invoiced before delivery, the balance sits in deferred revenue.
4. Where delivery precedes invoicing, an unbilled receivable is recorded.

## 6. Contract modifications

A modification is treated as a separate contract if it adds distinct services priced at standalone selling price. Otherwise the remaining consideration is reallocated over the remaining obligations. Modifications must be documented by the deal desk and approved by the Controller.

# Data Privacy and GDPR Compliance

## 1. Scope

This policy governs the processing of personal data of customers, employees, candidates and website visitors. It applies to every team and every system, including systems bought by a department without Legal involvement. Where local law is stricter than this policy, the stricter rule applies.

## 2. Lawful basis

Every processing activity needs a lawful basis recorded in the processing register: contract, legal obligation, legitimate interest, consent or vital interest. ## 3. Data subject rights

1. A data subject access request (DSAR) must be answered within 30 days of receipt.
2. The 30-day clock starts when the request reaches the privacy mailbox, not when the team begins work.

## 4. Breach notification

1. A suspected personal data breach must be reported to the DPO within 24 hours of discovery.
2. The DPO assesses whether the breach is notifiable; a notifiable breach is reported to the regulator within 72 hours.

New systems and features must complete a data protection impact assessment before launch where they process sensitive data, profile individuals or use new technology. The DPIA is reviewed by the DPO and stored with the project record.

## 7. Training and audit

All employees complete privacy training annually. The DPO audits two teams per quarter against the processing register and reports findings to the audit committee.

# Incident Response Runbook

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.
3. **Sev-3** — limited impact with a workaround.
4. **Sev-4** — cosmetic or single-user issue.

Severity is declared by the on-call engineer and may be raised by the incident commander at any time. Downgrading a Sev-1 requires the incident commander and the engineering director.

## 2. Response windows

| Step | Sev-1 | Sev-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge page | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Open incident channel | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Status page update | 30 minutes | 2 hours |
| Customer communication | 1 hour | 4 hours |

Missing an acknowledgement window is tracked as a reliability metric, not a disciplinary matter, unless it is repeated.

## 3. Roles

The incident commander owns the incident and does not debug. The communications lead writes status updates. The subject-matter engineers investigate. The scribe keeps the timeline. For a Sev-1, the incident commander is the on-call engineering manager; for a Sev-2 it may be the on-call engineer.

1. Acknowledge the page and declare severity in the incident channel.
2. Open the bridge. For a Sev-1, the bridge must open within 15 minutes of declaration; see Operations_Sev_Incident_Escalation for the current runbook version.
3. Assign the four roles.
4. Mitigate first, diagnose second. Roll back if the change is the suspected cause.
5. Update the status page at the intervals in Section 2.
6. Resolve only when the customer impact has ended, not when the root cause is understood.

## 5. Communication

Internal updates go in the incident channel every 30 minutes for a Sev-1 and every 2 hours for a Sev-2. Customer updates are written by the communications lead and approved by the incident commander. Never speculate about root cause in a customer update.

## 6. Postmortem

1. A postmortem is required for every Sev-1 and Sev-2.

# Vendor Security Review

## 1. When a review is required

Any third party that will store, process or access Meridian data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. This includes SaaS tools, contractors with system access, managed services and data processors. A review is not required for vendors that receive only Public information, but the classification must be recorded.

## 2. Process and timelines

1. The business owner submits the vendor request with the intended data classification and integration scope.
2. Security Engineering sends the standard questionnaire within 2 working days.
3. The vendor returns the questionnaire and evidence. The review concludes within 30 days of receiving complete evidence.
4. Reviews requiring a penetration test summary or a Data Processing Agreement take up to 45 days.
5. Contracts must not be signed before the review is recorded as passed.

## 3. Evidence requirements

1. SOC 2 Type II is required for any vendor processing Confidential or Restricted data. A SOC 2 Type I is accepted only with a remediation plan and a follow-up date.
2. ISO 27001 certification is accepted in place of SOC 2 where the scope covers the service in question.
3. Vendors without either certification require a documented compensating review by Security Engineering and approval from the CTO.
4. Encryption at rest and in transit must be evidenced.
5. Sub-processors must be listed and approved; unreported sub-processors are a contractual breach.

## 4. Data processing terms

Where personal data is involved, Legal_Data_Privacy_GDPR_Compliance requires a Data Processing Agreement. The DPA must cover purpose limitation, breach notification within 72 hours, deletion on termination and audit rights. Vendors that cannot accept the standard terms are escalated to Legal.

## 5. Ongoing monitoring

1. Confidential and Restricted vendors are reassessed annually.
2. A vendor security incident must be reported to Meridian within 72 hours under the DPA.
3. Access granted to vendor staff is reviewed quarterly with the vendor's named contacts.
4. Vendors that fail two consecutive reassessments are placed on a remediation plan and may be terminated by the business owner.

## 6. Exceptions

An exception requires the CTO's written approval, a compensating control and an expiry date no later than 90 days. Exceptions are reported to the security committee monthly.

Meridian moved to a hybrid model in 2022. Between 2022 and 2025 the expectation was set locally by each department, which produced inconsistent attendance and made desk planning unreliable. # Shift Handover Protocol

## 1. Purpose

Support and operations run three shifts. This protocol ensures nothing is lost between them. It applies to the service desk, the data centre operations team and the on-call rotation.

## 2. Overlap

1. Shifts overlap by 15 minutes.
2. The outgoing shift may not leave before the handover is acknowledged.

The handover sheet records: open tickets with priority, systems in a degraded state, changes in the last 24 hours, scheduled maintenance in the next 24 hours, and anything a customer is waiting on. It is written in the shared operations log, not in a personal note.

# 14-Day SLA Commitment

## 1. Commitment

Meridian commits to completing standard customer onboarding within 14 calendar days of receiving a complete setup package. The commitment applies to the Professional and Enterprise plans. Starter plan onboarding is self-service and is not covered.

## 2. Start and stop

1. The clock starts when the complete setup package is received: signed contract, admin contact, domain verification and data export specification.
2. The clock pauses while Meridian waits for customer input and resumes when the input arrives.
3. The clock does not pause for customer holidays, only for Meridian-declared freezes.
4. The clock stops when the production tenant is live and the admin receives the handover email.

## 3. Credits

1. If onboarding exceeds 14 days for reasons within Meridian's control, the customer receives a service credit of 5% of the first-year subscription fee.
2. A delay of more than 30 days attracts a 10% credit.
3. Credits are applied to the next invoice and are not paid in cash.
4. Credits are not available where the delay is caused by missing customer input, third-party integration delays outside Meridian's control, or a customer-requested change in scope.

## 4. Reporting

1. Onboarding status is reported weekly to Customer Operations.
2. Any account projected to miss the commitment is escalated to the delivery lead within 48 hours.
3. Monthly performance is published internally with the number of accounts, the median days to live and the credits issued.

## 5. Exceptions

Non-standard onboarding, including custom data migration and on-premises deployment, is scoped separately and is not covered by this commitment. Sales must not promise the 14-day commitment for non-standard onboarding without Customer Operations approval.

# Severity Incident Escalation

## 1. Purpose

This runbook defines who is paged, in what order, and how quickly a bridge must open when a production or customer-facing incident is declared. It is the operational companion to IT_Incident_Response_Runbook, which defines severity and the postmortem process.

## 2. Bridge requirement

Runbook version 1.4, in force from January 2025 until February 2026, required the incident bridge to open within 10 minutes of declaration. This version (2.0) requires the bridge to open within 15 minutes, because the 10-minute target produced incomplete bridges while pages were still in flight. The 15-minute window is the current standard and applies to every Sev-1, including security incidents.

## 3. Escalation matrix

| Severity | First page | Second page (after) | Executive notified |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sev-1 | On-call engineer, on-call manager | Engineering director (15 min) | CTO (30 min) |
| Sev-2 | On-call engineer | On-call manager (30 min) | Department head (2 h) |
| Sev-3 | On-call engineer | Team lead (next business day) | No |

Pages go through the on-call tool, not direct messages. If the first page is not acknowledged within the window, the tool automatically escalates to the next level. Escalation does not stop when someone joins the bridge; it stops when the incident commander is confirmed.

## 4. Roles on the bridge

The incident commander owns coordination and communication. The communications lead writes customer updates. The scribe keeps the timeline. Subject-matter engineers investigate. For a Sev-1 the incident commander must be an engineering manager or above; for a Sev-2 the on-call engineer may take the role.

## 5. Communication cadence

Internal updates every 30 minutes for a Sev-1 and every 2 hours for a Sev-2. Customer updates follow IT_Incident_Response_Runbook. No root-cause speculation in customer communication.

## 6. Declaring and downgrading

Any engineer may declare a Sev-1. Downgrading requires the incident commander and the engineering director. Repeatedly downgrading to avoid the bridge requirement is reviewed by Reliability Engineering.

## 7. After the incident

A postmortem is due within 5 business days.

# Data Privacy and GDPR Compliance

## 1. Scope

This policy governs the processing of personal data of customers, employees, candidates and website visitors. It applies to every team and every system, including systems bought by a department without Legal involvement. Where local law is stricter than this policy, the stricter rule applies.

## 2. Lawful basis

Every processing activity needs a lawful basis recorded in the processing register: contract, legal obligation, legitimate interest, consent or vital interest. Marketing consent must be opt-in and separately recorded; pre-ticked boxes are not consent. Legitimate interest assessments are documented by the DPO.

## 3. Data subject rights

1. A data subject access request (DSAR) must be answered within 30 days of receipt.
2. The 30-day clock starts when the request reaches the privacy mailbox, not when the team begins work.
3. Identity must be verified before data is released; verification must not require excessive documentation.
4. Erasure requests are honoured unless a legal retention obligation applies under Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule.
5. Requests are logged, and the log is reviewed monthly by the DPO.

## 4. Breach notification

1. A suspected personal data breach must be reported to the DPO within 24 hours of discovery.
2. The DPO assesses whether the breach is notifiable; a notifiable breach is reported to the regulator within 72 hours.
3. Affected individuals are informed without undue delay where the breach is likely to result in high risk.
4. A breach log is maintained for five years.

## 5. Vendors and transfers

Vendors processing personal data require a Data Processing Agreement under IT_Vendor_Security_Review. Transfers outside the EEA require an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses. A transfer impact assessment is required for any new destination country.

## 6. Privacy by design

New systems and features must complete a data protection impact assessment before launch where they process sensitive data, profile individuals or use new technology. The DPIA is reviewed by the DPO and stored with the project record.

## 7. Training and audit

All employees complete privacy training annually. The DPO audits two teams per quarter against the processing register and reports findings to the audit committee.

## 8. Related documents

- IT_Data_Classification_Standard for data tiers.
- Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule for retention.
- IT_Vendor_Security_Review for vendor DPAs.

# Incident Response Runbook

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.
3. **Sev-3** — limited impact with a workaround.
4. **Sev-4** — cosmetic or single-user issue.

Severity is declared by the on-call engineer and may be raised by the incident commander at any time. Downgrading a Sev-1 requires the incident commander and the engineering director.

## 2. Response windows

| Step | Sev-1 | Sev-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge page | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Open incident channel | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Status page update | 30 minutes | 2 hours |
| Customer communication | 1 hour | 4 hours |

Missing an acknowledgement window is tracked as a reliability metric, not a disciplinary matter, unless it is repeated.

## 3. Roles

The incident commander owns the incident and does not debug. The communications lead writes status updates. The subject-matter engineers investigate. The scribe keeps the timeline. For a Sev-1, the incident commander is the on-call engineering manager; for a Sev-2 it may be the on-call engineer.

## 4. Process

1. Acknowledge the page and declare severity in the incident channel.
2. Open the bridge. For a Sev-1, the bridge must open within 15 minutes of declaration; see Operations_Sev_Incident_Escalation for the current runbook version.
3. Assign the four roles.
4. Mitigate first, diagnose second. Roll back if the change is the suspected cause.
5. Update the status page at the intervals in Section 2.
6. Resolve only when the customer impact has ended, not when the root cause is understood.

## 5. Communication

Internal updates go in the incident channel every 30 minutes for a Sev-1 and every 2 hours for a Sev-2. Customer updates are written by the communications lead and approved by the incident commander. Never speculate about root cause in a customer update.

## 6. Postmortem

1. A postmortem is required for every Sev-1 and Sev-2.

## 1. Scope

This process covers every agreement Meridian signs with a third party: customer contracts, vendor agreements, NDAs, data processing agreements, leases and statements of work. Employment contracts are handled by People Operations and are not reviewed here.

1. Standard contract review takes 7 business days from receipt of a complete request.

Legal reviews liability caps, indemnities, termination rights, data protection, payment terms, governing law and intellectual property. # Subpoena and Litigation Hold

## 1. Immediate steps

1. Anyone who receives a subpoena, court order, regulatory request or formal notice of a dispute must notify Legal within 24 hours.
2. Do not respond to the requester, confirm receipt, or discuss the matter outside Legal.
3. Do not delete, edit or move any related record, including chat messages, emails and tickets.
4. Legal appoints a single point of contact for the matter.

## 2. Litigation hold

1. Legal issues a written hold to the custodians it identifies.
2. Custodians must acknowledge the hold within two business days.
3. The hold suspends every deletion rule in Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule, including automated purge jobs.
4. IT must suspend mailbox and backup deletion for the named custodians until Legal releases the hold.
5. Any loss of data after a hold is issued must be reported to Legal immediately.

## 3. Preservation scope

Preservation covers documents, emails, chat, tickets, code repositories, meeting recordings and device data. Legal defines the date range and custodian list; anything outside the range is not preserved but must not be destroyed if it may become relevant.

## 4. Collection and review

Collection is performed by IT at Legal's direction, with a documented chain of custody. Review is conducted by Legal and, where required, external counsel. Access to collected material is limited to the matter team.

## 5. Confidentiality

The existence of a subpoena is confidential and must not be discussed with customers, vendors or colleagues outside the matter team unless Legal approves. Breach of confidentiality can itself create legal exposure.

## 6. Release

Legal releases the hold in writing when the matter concludes. Normal retention resumes from the release date, and the retention clock is not shortened by the hold period.

## 7. Related documents

- Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule for normal retention.
- IT_Data_Classification_Standard for data handling.
- IT_Acceptable_Use_Policy for communication channels in scope.
- Legal_Data_Privacy_GDPR_Compliance for personal data in collected material.

## 8. Version history

Version 2.2 added the chat and code repository scope. Version 2.1 set the 24-hour notification window. Questions go to Legal.

# Data Privacy and GDPR Compliance

## 1. Scope

This policy governs the processing of personal data of customers, employees, candidates and website visitors. It applies to every team and every system, including systems bought by a department without Legal involvement. Where local law is stricter than this policy, the stricter rule applies.

## 2. Lawful basis

Every processing activity needs a lawful basis recorded in the processing register: contract, legal obligation, legitimate interest, consent or vital interest. Marketing consent must be opt-in and separately recorded; pre-ticked boxes are not consent. Legitimate interest assessments are documented by the DPO.

## 3. Data subject rights

1. A data subject access request (DSAR) must be answered within 30 days of receipt.
2. The 30-day clock starts when the request reaches the privacy mailbox, not when the team begins work.
3. Identity must be verified before data is released; verification must not require excessive documentation.
4. Erasure requests are honoured unless a legal retention obligation applies under Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule.
5. Requests are logged, and the log is reviewed monthly by the DPO.

## 4. Breach notification

1. A suspected personal data breach must be reported to the DPO within 24 hours of discovery.
2. The DPO assesses whether the breach is notifiable; a notifiable breach is reported to the regulator within 72 hours.
3. Affected individuals are informed without undue delay where the breach is likely to result in high risk.
4. A breach log is maintained for five years.

## 5. Vendors and transfers

Vendors processing personal data require a Data Processing Agreement under IT_Vendor_Security_Review. Transfers outside the EEA require an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses. A transfer impact assessment is required for any new destination country.

## 6. Privacy by design

New systems and features must complete a data protection impact assessment before launch where they process sensitive data, profile individuals or use new technology. The DPIA is reviewed by the DPO and stored with the project record.

## 7. Training and audit

All employees complete privacy training annually. The DPO audits two teams per quarter against the processing register and reports findings to the audit committee.

## 8. Related documents

- IT_Data_Classification_Standard for data tiers.
- Legal_Records_Retention_Schedule for retention.
- IT_Vendor_Security_Review for vendor DPAs.

# Incident Response Runbook

## 1. Severity definitions

1. **Sev-1** — customer-facing outage or data loss affecting more than 20% of customers, or any confirmed security breach.
2. **Sev-2** — degraded service affecting a material subset of customers, or an internal system blocking a revenue process.
3. **Sev-3** — limited impact with a workaround.
4. **Sev-4** — cosmetic or single-user issue.

Severity is declared by the on-call engineer and may be raised by the incident commander at any time. Downgrading a Sev-1 requires the incident commander and the engineering director.

## 2. Response windows

| Step | Sev-1 | Sev-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge page | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Open incident channel | 15 minutes | 1 hour |
| Status page update | 30 minutes | 2 hours |
| Customer communication | 1 hour | 4 hours |

Missing an acknowledgement window is tracked as a reliability metric, not a disciplinary matter, unless it is repeated.

## 3. Roles

The incident commander owns the incident and does not debug. The communications lead writes status updates. The subject-matter engineers investigate. The scribe keeps the timeline. For a Sev-1, the incident commander is the on-call engineering manager; for a Sev-2 it may be the on-call engineer.

## 4. Process

1. Acknowledge the page and declare severity in the incident channel.
2. Open the bridge. For a Sev-1, the bridge must open within 15 minutes of declaration; see Operations_Sev_Incident_Escalation for the current runbook version.
3. Assign the four roles.
4. Mitigate first, diagnose second. Roll back if the change is the suspected cause.
5. Update the status page at the intervals in Section 2.
6. Resolve only when the customer impact has ended, not when the root cause is understood.

## 5. Communication

Internal updates go in the incident channel every 30 minutes for a Sev-1 and every 2 hours for a Sev-2. Customer updates are written by the communications lead and approved by the incident commander. Never speculate about root cause in a customer update.

## 6. Postmortem

1. A postmortem is required for every Sev-1 and Sev-2.

Onboarding runs through five stages: contract handover, environment provisioning, data import, configuration and acceptance, and go-live handover. # Severity Incident Escalation

## 1. Purpose

This runbook defines who is paged, in what order, and how quickly a bridge must open when a production or customer-facing incident is declared. It is the operational companion to IT_Incident_Response_Runbook, which defines severity and the postmortem process.

## 2. Bridge requirement

Runbook version 1.4, in force from January 2025 until February 2026, required the incident bridge to open within 10 minutes of declaration. This version (2.0) requires the bridge to open within 15 minutes, because the 10-minute target produced incomplete bridges while pages were still in flight. The 15-minute window is the current standard and applies to every Sev-1, including security incidents.

## 3. Escalation matrix

| Severity | First page | Second page (after) | Executive notified |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sev-1 | On-call engineer, on-call manager | Engineering director (15 min) | CTO (30 min) |
| Sev-2 | On-call engineer | On-call manager (30 min) | Department head (2 h) |
| Sev-3 | On-call engineer | Team lead (next business day) | No |

Pages go through the on-call tool, not direct messages. If the first page is not acknowledged within the window, the tool automatically escalates to the next level. Escalation does not stop when someone joins the bridge; it stops when the incident commander is confirmed.

## 4. Roles on the bridge

The incident commander owns coordination and communication. The communications lead writes customer updates. The scribe keeps the timeline. Subject-matter engineers investigate. For a Sev-1 the incident commander must be an engineering manager or above; for a Sev-2 the on-call engineer may take the role.

## 5. Communication cadence

Internal updates every 30 minutes for a Sev-1 and every 2 hours for a Sev-2. Customer updates follow IT_Incident_Response_Runbook. No root-cause speculation in customer communication.

## 6. Declaring and downgrading

Any engineer may declare a Sev-1. Downgrading requires the incident commander and the engineering director. Repeatedly downgrading to avoid the bridge requirement is reviewed by Reliability Engineering.

## 7. After the incident

A postmortem is due within 5 business days.

This process covers every agreement Meridian signs with a third party: customer contracts, vendor agreements, NDAs, data processing agreements, leases and statements of work. Employment contracts are handled by People Operations and are not reviewed here.

1. Standard contract review takes 7 business days from receipt of a complete request.

3. Attach the counterparty's draft and any redlines already exchanged.
4. State the deadline and the consequence of missing it.

Legal reviews liability caps, indemnities, termination rights, data protection, payment terms, governing law and intellectual property. Any clause that deviates from the playbook requires a documented approval from the Head of Legal. Unlimited liability, most-favoured-nation pricing and exclusivity are escalation triggers.
